summary: Tested the Codex lead from #374: derive STMT-ACT-SIMPLY-PRIOR-TO-POTENCY over the existing predicates from 'every potency is being actualized' and the mover's priority, with STMT-NOTHING-REDUCED-TO-ACT-EXCEPT-BY-A-MOVER and STMT-NOTHING-MOVES-EXCEPT-AS-IN-ACT. The lead's 'MovesIn y x r -> PriorSimply y x' was replaced by the weaker existing bridge STMT-ACTUAL-MOVER-IS-SIMPLY-PRIOR plus STMT-NOTHING-IN-ACT-AND-POTENCY-IN-SAME-RESPECT (which excludes the self-mover). The derivation is valid and each of the five premises is needed (ACT-PRIOR-FROM-MOTION-FACTS). Source search for 'every potency is being actualized': Physics III.1 (ARIST-PHYS-III-1, materialized and read whole, 200b12-201b15) defines motion as the actuality of the potential qua such and says a thing is moved only while that actuality is present, 'for each thing can be active at one time and not at another, as the buildable' (201b8-9); that denies the premise, and is recorded as claim ARIST-PHYS-201B-POTENCY-NOT-ALWAYS-ACTIVE-A. Aquinas' ST I q.2 a.3 states only the converse (nihil movetur nisi secundum quod est in potentia), and the case's reading of q.3 a.1 already says act's priority does not make every potency a present being-moved. Rejected reading: taking Physics III.1, 201a10-11 (motion is the actuality of the potential) as saying every potential is in motion; it defines motion and says nothing of potentials not being actualized. Without the premise, the other four yield priority only for potencies being actualized, which does not reach ST I q.3 a.1's use: a model of every prima via premise, the bridge and a dormant potency has a first mover moved by none, first being, in potency. The mover-priority bridge itself stays unsourced (ATTEMPT-MET-IX-8-ACTUAL-MOVER-PRIORITY). No argument for STMT-ACT-SIMPLY-PRIOR-TO-POTENCY was added: it would add two bare premises to the root paths and close nothing, since sourced leaves stay leaves.
blocker: The content of act's simple priority beyond potencies being actualized concerns dormant potencies, including any in a first unmoved being. A derivation needs a sourced premise about those (for example Met. IX.8, 1050b6-8 read for every potency, or a sourced 'every potency is a potency of something generated by an actual being' from IX.8, 1049b17-29 with a priority that is simple, not temporal), or the root's use must be replaced by one that does not apply priority to an unmoved being.
